title: Latest scam: Walmart gift card text message

asr.full_text: ALL OVER THE VALLEY RECENTLY GOT A TEXT MESSAGE THAT SAYS THEY WANT A THOUSAND DOLLAR GIFT CARD FROM WALMART. THE PROBLEM WASN'T TRUE.. TINA JENSON HAS MORE ON WHY YOU DON'T WANT TO CLICK ON THE LINK. THAT'S RIGHT... THE SENDER WASN'T TRYING TO GIVE YOU MONEY... IN FACT, LIKE ALL SCAMS, THEY WERE TRYING TO TAKE YOUR MONEY. SEVERAL OF US IN THE NEWSROOM RECEIVED THE MESSAGE. IT COMES FROM A 2-O-2 AREA CODE AND SENDS INSTRUCTIONS TO CLICK ON A LINK TO CLAIM THE CARD. to take your money. Several of us in the newsroom received the message, it comes from a 202 area code and sends instructions to click the link to claim this card. But people who've clicked on the message, say it asks for your credit information to pay for shipping and handling. We'd love to find a way to stop this, however there isn't a way, because there are computer systems set up around the world generating random phone numbers, sending these texts out. If you receive this, you are one of a million, you're not one in a million and trying to track that computer down and shut it down is nearly impossible. VO EVEN IF YOU DON'T ENTER YOUR CREDIT CARD INFORMATION, CLICKING ON A LINK COULD DOWNLOAD A VIRUS ONTO YOUR COMPUTER. SO IF YOU GET A UNSOLICITED TEXT MESSAGE THAT YOU'VE WON A GIFT CARD, THE BEST THING YOU CAN DO IS HIT DELETE. LIVE IN THE STUDIO, TINA JENSEN, TODAY'S CHANNEL6 NEWS. the best thing you can do is hit Delete. Live in the studio, Tina Jensen here in the Newsroom. At 7 30 tm, We go a second look at what happens when you have a send to text message that just says you've won a gift card. Here in the studio, Tina Jensen for Channel 6.

textual.observation: A reported text message promises a $1,000 Walmart gift card, directs recipients to click a link to claim it, and is described as requesting credit information for shipping and handling.

evidence.quote: A THOUSAND DOLLAR GIFT CARD FROM WALMART
sends instructions to click the link to claim this card.
it asks for your credit information to pay for shipping and handling.

textual.context: Presented in a news-report and consumer-warning context rather than as a direct promotion by the speaker.
textual.potential_relevance: The promised gift card is directly linked to clicking a link and potentially submitting credit information for a stated shipping-related payment, creating a reward-to-action-to-data/payment relationship for later context assessment.
textual.limitations: These records do not independently verify the sender, link destination, requested payment, identity of the message sender, or any actual data submission or financial loss. ASR may contain transcription errors.

visual.observation: A text message and accompanying webpage visibly promise a free $1,000 Walmart gift card and instruct the recipient to enter “FREE” or “1000” at the displayed external URL, with the broadcast lower-third labeling it “TEXT MESSAGE SCAM.”
visual.context: The material is presented within a television news segment discussing the message; the Walmart branding and gift-card offer appear in the depicted message/webpage, while the broadcast labels the segment “TEXT MESSAGE SCAM.”
visual.potential_relevance: The high-value gift-card promise is directly linked to entering a code and visiting an external web address, while the offer uses Walmart branding; this relationship may merit review as a described text-message scam mechanism.
visual.limitations: The sampled frames do not establish who operated the destination, whether the URL was reachable, what information or payment steps followed, or whether any recipient received or lost funds.

textual_context_notes.observation: The report advises recipients of an unsolicited gift-card message to delete it.

evidence.quote: SO IF YOU GET A UNSOLICITED TEXT MESSAGE THAT YOU'VE WON A GIFT CARD, THE BEST THING YOU CAN DO IS HIT DELETE.

textual_context_notes.observation: The report warns that clicking the link could have a device-related consequence even without entering credit-card information.

evidence.quote: CLICKING ON A LINK COULD DOWNLOAD A VIRUS ONTO YOUR COMPUTER.

visual_context_notes.observation: The segment is framed as a television news report, with ABC 6/KIVI branding and a Better Business Bureau representative, Dale Dixon, shown as an interview subject.
The broadcast repeatedly displays the on-screen label “TEXT MESSAGE SCAM” while showing the gift-card message and webpage.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it presents the Walmart gift-card message and claim link as the subject of a television news report and consumer warning, rather than as an offer from the presenter or broadcaster. The segment advises viewers to delete unsolicited gift-card messages and includes a Better Business Bureau interview subject as part of the reporting.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The segment examines a purported gift-card message and its link, reports an attributed credit-information request and warns viewers not to click and to delete unsolicited messages.

evidence.observation: The report introduces an examination of why viewers should not click the message link.
evidence.quote: TINA JENSON HAS MORE ON WHY YOU DON'T WANT TO CLICK ON THE LINK.

evidence.observation: The report attributes to people who clicked the message the account that it asks for credit information for shipping and handling.
evidence.quote: people who've clicked on the message, say it asks for your credit information to pay for shipping and handling.

evidence.observation: The report advises deleting an unsolicited message claiming the recipient won a gift card.
evidence.quote: SO IF YOU GET A UNSOLICITED TEXT MESSAGE THAT YOU'VE WON A GIFT CARD, THE BEST THING YOU CAN DO IS HIT DELETE.

evidence.observation: The report warns that clicking the link could download a virus.
evidence.quote: CLICKING ON A LINK COULD DOWNLOAD A VIRUS ONTO YOUR COMPUTER.

evidence.observation: The reported message directs recipients to click a link to claim the card.
evidence.quote: sends instructions to click the link to claim this card.

evidence.observation: A news presenter stands beside a displayed message offering a Walmart gift card and directing the viewer to a web address.
A phone message displaying a gift-card claim and web link appears with the broadcast lower-third text “TEXT MESSAGE SCAM.”
An interview subject appears with a lower-third identifying him as Dale Dixon of the Better Business Bureau.
